    • SEC-SSS3-COVER

    1. Scenario suite coverage

     UID: SEC-SSS3-COVER
    Operating scenarios exercise the patented iron-air plant. Charge, discharge, and
    LODES durations follow US12308414B2 (8 h to seasonal, including about 100 h and
    300 h). Chemistry faults follow EP4602674A1 HER competition, magnetite conversion,
    and thick-electrode transport. Air and mechanical faults follow US12308414B2
    flooding, dry-out, sparging, fan/pump, and containment disclosures. Software
    scenario results are not hardware validation of either patent.
    IA-NBK-007
    1.1. Charge scenarios UID: IA-NBK-007 STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Child):
    • IA-SCN-CHG-CC Constant-current charging
    • IA-SCN-CHG-CP Constant-power charging
    • IA-SCN-CHG-CV Constant-voltage charging
    • IA-SCN-CHG-TAPER Charge tapering
    • IA-SCN-CHG-PARTIAL Partial charge
    • IA-SCN-CHG-TERM Charge termination
    • IA-SCN-CHG-OVER Overcharge protection
    • IA-SCN-CHG-LOWT Low-temperature charging
    • IA-SCN-CHG-HIGHT High-temperature charging
    • IA-SCN-CHG-HER Charging with hydrogen evolution
    • IA-SCN-CHG-LOWFLOW Charging with limited electrolyte circulation
    STATEMENT: Required charge scenarios: constant-current, constant-power, constant-voltage,
    charge tapering, partial charge, charge termination, overcharge protection,
    low-temperature charging, high-temperature charging, charging with hydrogen
    evolution, and charging with limited electrolyte circulation.

    Charge current greater than 6 mA/g to at least twice rated capacity SHALL be an
    allowed formation/full-charge protocol (EP4602674A1 [0261]). Dual-electrode charge
    SHALL use the OER path (EP4602674A1 [0049]).
     RATIONALE: US12308414B2 rechargeable metal-air operation; EP4602674A1 charge through OER and
    HER competition on thick iron electrodes.
     COMMENT: Each listed scenario has a unique IA-SCN-CHG-* ID, Python scenario function, notebook,
    and seaborn plots.
    • IA-SCN-CHG-CC
      2.1. Constant-current charging UID: IA-SCN-CHG-CC STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-007 Charge scenarios
      STATEMENT: Apply a constant charging current and record voltage, SOC, HER, and temperature.
       COMMENT: SOC increases. Terminal voltage rises. Current remains at the commanded charge value
      until a termination limit.
    • IA-SCN-CHG-CP
      2.2. Constant-power charging UID: IA-SCN-CHG-CP STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-007 Charge scenarios
      STATEMENT: Apply a constant charging power command.
       COMMENT: Electrical power tracks the charge setpoint within solver tolerance until limits.
    • IA-SCN-CHG-CV
      2.3. Constant-voltage charging UID: IA-SCN-CHG-CV STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-007 Charge scenarios
      STATEMENT: Hold a constant charge voltage after a current-limited approach.
       COMMENT: Charge current tapers as SOC increases under CV hold.
    • IA-SCN-CHG-TAPER
      2.4. Charge tapering UID: IA-SCN-CHG-TAPER STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-007 Charge scenarios
      STATEMENT: Execute CC-CV tapering to a cutoff current.
       COMMENT: Simulation stops or flags complete when abs(I) falls below cutoff while voltage is held.
    • IA-SCN-CHG-PARTIAL
      2.5. Partial charge UID: IA-SCN-CHG-PARTIAL STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-007 Charge scenarios
      STATEMENT: Charge from an intermediate SOC to a higher intermediate SOC.
       COMMENT: Final SOC is between the start SOC and 1.0 and matches the scheduled stop.
    • IA-SCN-CHG-TERM
      2.6. Charge termination UID: IA-SCN-CHG-TERM STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-007 Charge scenarios
      STATEMENT: Terminate charge on voltage, current, SOC, or hydrogen-rate limits.
       COMMENT: Supervisory controller enters a rest or protection mode when a documented limit is crossed.
    • IA-SCN-CHG-OVER
      2.7. Overcharge protection UID: IA-SCN-CHG-OVER STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-007 Charge scenarios
      STATEMENT: Attempt overcharge and verify protection action.
       COMMENT: Current is removed or limited after the overcharge threshold. HER may rise before trip.
    • IA-SCN-CHG-LOWT
      2.8. Low-temperature charging UID: IA-SCN-CHG-LOWT STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-007 Charge scenarios
      STATEMENT: Charge at a cold ambient temperature within the property-model domain.
       COMMENT: Polarization is larger than the 298 K reference case. Solver remains stable.
    • IA-SCN-CHG-HIGHT
      2.9. High-temperature charging UID: IA-SCN-CHG-HIGHT STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-007 Charge scenarios
      STATEMENT: Charge at an elevated ambient temperature within the property-model domain.
       COMMENT: HER rate is higher than the 298 K reference at the same current.
    • IA-SCN-CHG-HER
      2.10. Charging with hydrogen evolution UID: IA-SCN-CHG-HER STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-007 Charge scenarios
      STATEMENT: Charge under conditions that produce measurable HER.
       COMMENT: H2 inventory increases. Faradaic efficiency of iron conversion is less than 1.
    • IA-SCN-CHG-LOWFLOW
      2.11. Charging with limited electrolyte circulation UID: IA-SCN-CHG-LOWFLOW STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-007 Charge scenarios
      STATEMENT: Charge with reduced or zero electrolyte pump flow.
       COMMENT: Local concentration gradients or voltage penalty exceed the circulating reference case.
    IA-NBK-008
    1.2. Discharge scenarios UID: IA-NBK-008 STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Child):
    • IA-SCN-DCH-CC Constant-current discharge
    • IA-SCN-DCH-CP Constant-power discharge
    • IA-SCN-DCH-VAR Variable-load discharge
    • IA-SCN-DCH-PARTIAL Partial discharge
    • IA-SCN-DCH-DEEP Deep discharge
    • IA-SCN-DCH-O2LIM Oxygen-limited discharge
    • IA-SCN-DCH-THMLIM Thermal-limited discharge
    • IA-SCN-DCH-HIGHRATE High-rate discharge
    • IA-SCN-DCH-LOWRATE Low-rate discharge
    • IA-SCN-DCH-100H 100-hour discharge
    STATEMENT: Required discharge scenarios: constant-current, constant-power, variable-load,
    partial discharge, deep discharge, oxygen-limited, thermal-limited, high-rate,
    low-rate, and 100-hour discharge.

    Discharge SHALL use the ORR path (EP4602674A1 [0049]). 100 h and 300 h discharges
    SHALL be available, corresponding to about 3-5 cm and 4-6 cm anode thickness in
    US12308414B2. Oxygen-limited discharge SHALL include restricted pO2 within
    0.01-100 atm (US12308414B2).
     RATIONALE: US12308414B2 duration versus anode thickness; EP4602674A1 dual-electrode discharge
    to Fe(OH)2 / Fe3O4.
     COMMENT: Each listed scenario has a unique IA-SCN-DCH-* ID, Python scenario function, and notebook.
    • IA-SCN-DCH-CC
      3.1. Constant-current discharge UID: IA-SCN-DCH-CC STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-008 Discharge scenarios
      STATEMENT: Apply a constant discharge current.
       COMMENT: SOC decreases. Voltage falls. Iron inventory is oxidized.
    • IA-SCN-DCH-CP
      3.2. Constant-power discharge UID: IA-SCN-DCH-CP STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-008 Discharge scenarios
      STATEMENT: Apply a constant discharge power command.
       COMMENT: Power tracks the discharge setpoint until a voltage or SOC limit.
    • IA-SCN-DCH-VAR
      3.3. Variable-load discharge UID: IA-SCN-DCH-VAR STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-008 Discharge scenarios
      STATEMENT: Apply a time-varying discharge load profile.
       COMMENT: Current follows the scheduled profile within solver tolerance.
    • IA-SCN-DCH-PARTIAL
      3.4. Partial discharge UID: IA-SCN-DCH-PARTIAL STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-008 Discharge scenarios
      STATEMENT: Discharge from a high SOC to an intermediate SOC.
       COMMENT: Final SOC matches the scheduled stop within tolerance.
    • IA-SCN-DCH-DEEP
      3.5. Deep discharge UID: IA-SCN-DCH-DEEP STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-008 Discharge scenarios
      STATEMENT: Discharge toward a low-SOC cutoff.
       COMMENT: Voltage declines and a low-SOC or low-voltage stop is reached without negative inventories.
    • IA-SCN-DCH-O2LIM
      3.6. Oxygen-limited discharge UID: IA-SCN-DCH-O2LIM STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-008 Discharge scenarios
      STATEMENT: Discharge with restricted oxygen supply.
       COMMENT: Available discharge current or voltage is lower than the air-rich reference.
    • IA-SCN-DCH-THMLIM
      3.7. Thermal-limited discharge UID: IA-SCN-DCH-THMLIM STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-008 Discharge scenarios
      STATEMENT: Discharge until a thermal protection limit.
       COMMENT: Controller reduces current or trips when temperature exceeds the documented limit.
    • IA-SCN-DCH-HIGHRATE
      3.8. High-rate discharge UID: IA-SCN-DCH-HIGHRATE STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-008 Discharge scenarios
      STATEMENT: Discharge at a high C-rate relative to the design current.
       COMMENT: Overpotential and heat generation exceed the low-rate case.
    • IA-SCN-DCH-LOWRATE
      3.9. Low-rate discharge UID: IA-SCN-DCH-LOWRATE STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-008 Discharge scenarios
      STATEMENT: Discharge at a low C-rate.
       COMMENT: Voltage remains closer to Nernst than the high-rate case.
    • IA-SCN-DCH-100H
      3.10. 100-hour discharge UID: IA-SCN-DCH-100H STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-008 Discharge scenarios
      STATEMENT: Discharge energy over a 100-hour window.
       COMMENT: Simulation spans 3.6e5 s and SOC declines monotonically under a positive discharge load.
    IA-NBK-009
    1.3. Transition scenarios UID: IA-NBK-009 STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Child):
    • IA-SCN-TRN-CHG2DCH Charge to discharge
    • IA-SCN-TRN-DCH2CHG Discharge to charge
    • IA-SCN-TRN-REVERSAL Rapid power reversal
    • IA-SCN-TRN-REST Rest period
    • IA-SCN-TRN-RELAX Voltage relaxation
    • IA-SCN-TRN-CYCLE Repeated cycling
    • IA-SCN-TRN-STARTUP Startup
    • IA-SCN-TRN-SHUTDOWN Shutdown
    • IA-SCN-TRN-RESTART Restart after protection trip
    STATEMENT: Required transition scenarios: charge to discharge, discharge to charge, rapid power
    reversal, rest period, voltage relaxation, repeated cycling, startup, shutdown, and
    restart after protection trip.

    Charge/discharge transitions SHALL operate the EP4602674A1 [0049] / US12308414B2
    FIGS. 5A-5B electrode switch, including electrical isolation of ORR during OER
    to protect the air electrode.
     COMMENT: Each listed scenario has a unique IA-SCN-TRN-* ID, Python scenario function, and notebook.
    • IA-SCN-TRN-CHG2DCH
      4.1. Charge to discharge UID: IA-SCN-TRN-CHG2DCH STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-009 Transition scenarios
      STATEMENT: Transition from charge to discharge.
       COMMENT: Current sign reverses. No nonphysical voltage spike is left unreported.
    • IA-SCN-TRN-DCH2CHG
      4.2. Discharge to charge UID: IA-SCN-TRN-DCH2CHG STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-009 Transition scenarios
      STATEMENT: Transition from discharge to charge.
       COMMENT: Current sign reverses. SOC slope changes sign.
    • IA-SCN-TRN-REVERSAL
      4.3. Rapid power reversal UID: IA-SCN-TRN-REVERSAL STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-009 Transition scenarios
      STATEMENT: Reverse power on a short time scale relative to thermal states.
       COMMENT: Electrical states respond faster than thermal states. Solver remains stable.
    • IA-SCN-TRN-REST
      4.4. Rest period UID: IA-SCN-TRN-REST STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-009 Transition scenarios
      STATEMENT: Hold zero applied current after operation.
       COMMENT: Terminal current is ~0. Voltage relaxes toward equilibrium.
    • IA-SCN-TRN-RELAX
      4.5. Voltage relaxation UID: IA-SCN-TRN-RELAX STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-009 Transition scenarios
      STATEMENT: Record open-circuit voltage relaxation after current interruption.
       COMMENT: The absolute value of dV/dt decreases with time during rest.
    • IA-SCN-TRN-CYCLE
      4.6. Repeated cycling UID: IA-SCN-TRN-CYCLE STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-009 Transition scenarios
      STATEMENT: Apply repeated charge/discharge cycles.
       COMMENT: SOC oscillates. Optional degradation states are nondecreasing.
    • IA-SCN-TRN-STARTUP
      4.7. Startup UID: IA-SCN-TRN-STARTUP STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-009 Transition scenarios
      STATEMENT: Start auxiliaries and electrical conversion from a rest state.
       COMMENT: Fan/pump speeds rise from near zero. DC bus voltage is established.
    • IA-SCN-TRN-SHUTDOWN
      4.8. Shutdown UID: IA-SCN-TRN-SHUTDOWN STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-009 Transition scenarios
      STATEMENT: Command a controlled shutdown.
       COMMENT: Power command goes to zero and auxiliaries decelerate.
    • IA-SCN-TRN-RESTART
      4.9. Restart after protection trip UID: IA-SCN-TRN-RESTART STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-009 Transition scenarios
      STATEMENT: Clear a protection trip and resume operation.
       COMMENT: Mode returns from protection to a documented operating mode without hidden-state cheating.
    IA-NBK-010
    1.4. Chemistry scenarios UID: IA-NBK-010 STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Child):
    • IA-SCN-CHM-PASS Iron passivation
    • IA-SCN-CHM-MAG Magnetite formation
    • IA-SCN-CHM-HER Hydrogen evolution chemistry scenario
    • IA-SCN-CHM-O2STARV Oxygen starvation
    • IA-SCN-CHM-CARB Carbonate accumulation
    • IA-SCN-CHM-H2ODEP Water depletion
    • IA-SCN-CHM-DILUTE Electrolyte dilution
    • IA-SCN-CHM-CONC Electrolyte concentration increase
    • IA-SCN-CHM-AGE Electrode aging
    • IA-SCN-CHM-CATDEG Catalyst degradation
    STATEMENT: Required chemistry scenarios: iron passivation, magnetite formation, hydrogen evolution,
    oxygen starvation, carbonate accumulation, water depletion, electrolyte dilution,
    electrolyte concentration increase, electrode aging, and catalyst degradation.

    Chemistry scenarios SHALL include planar versus channeled versus interdigitated
    coulombic-efficiency comparison at 6 M KOH and 303 K (EP4602674A1 FIGS. 19-27)
    and carbonate clogging of air-electrode pores (US12308414B2).
     COMMENT: Each listed scenario has a unique IA-SCN-CHM-* ID, Python scenario function, and notebook.
    • IA-SCN-CHM-PASS
      5.1. Iron passivation UID: IA-SCN-CHM-PASS STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-010 Chemistry scenarios
      STATEMENT: Exercise passivation-thickness growth.
       COMMENT: Active area or exchange current declines as passivation thickness grows.
    • IA-SCN-CHM-MAG
      5.2. Magnetite formation UID: IA-SCN-CHM-MAG STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-010 Chemistry scenarios
      STATEMENT: Convert Fe(OH)2 toward Fe3O4.
       COMMENT: Fe3O4 inventory increases and Fe(OH)2 decreases with conserved iron atoms.
    • IA-SCN-CHM-HER
      5.3. Hydrogen evolution chemistry scenario UID: IA-SCN-CHM-HER STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-010 Chemistry scenarios
      STATEMENT: Isolate HER kinetics versus potential.
       COMMENT: H2 production increases as iron potential becomes more negative.
    • IA-SCN-CHM-O2STARV
      5.4. Oxygen starvation UID: IA-SCN-CHM-O2STARV STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-010 Chemistry scenarios
      STATEMENT: Remove oxygen supply during discharge.
       COMMENT: ORR current collapses as O2 inventory approaches the documented floor.
    • IA-SCN-CHM-CARB
      5.5. Carbonate accumulation UID: IA-SCN-CHM-CARB STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-010 Chemistry scenarios
      STATEMENT: Expose electrolyte to CO2-bearing air.
       COMMENT: CO3 inventory increases and OH- inventory decreases.
    • IA-SCN-CHM-H2ODEP
      5.6. Water depletion UID: IA-SCN-CHM-H2ODEP STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-010 Chemistry scenarios
      STATEMENT: Operate with net water consumption or evaporation.
       COMMENT: Water inventory declines and is flagged before becoming negative.
    • IA-SCN-CHM-DILUTE
      5.7. Electrolyte dilution UID: IA-SCN-CHM-DILUTE STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-010 Chemistry scenarios
      STATEMENT: Add water or reduce KOH inventory.
       COMMENT: KOH concentration and conductivity decrease.
    • IA-SCN-CHM-CONC
      5.8. Electrolyte concentration increase UID: IA-SCN-CHM-CONC STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-010 Chemistry scenarios
      STATEMENT: Remove water or add KOH.
       COMMENT: KOH concentration increases within the property-model domain.
    • IA-SCN-CHM-AGE
      5.9. Electrode aging UID: IA-SCN-CHM-AGE STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-010 Chemistry scenarios
      STATEMENT: Apply aging rates to iron active material.
       COMMENT: Available capacity declines irreversibly.
    • IA-SCN-CHM-CATDEG
      5.10. Catalyst degradation UID: IA-SCN-CHM-CATDEG STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-010 Chemistry scenarios
      STATEMENT: Decay ORR/OER catalyst activity.
       COMMENT: Exchange current densities decrease over time under the aging model.
    IA-NBK-011
    1.5. Environmental scenarios UID: IA-NBK-011 STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Child):
    • IA-SCN-ENV-COLD Cold start
    • IA-SCN-ENV-HOT Hot start
    • IA-SCN-ENV-TAMP Ambient temperature cycling
    • IA-SCN-ENV-HIGHRH High relative humidity
    • IA-SCN-ENV-LOWRH Low relative humidity
    • IA-SCN-ENV-ALT High altitude
    • IA-SCN-ENV-LOWO2 Reduced atmospheric oxygen
    • IA-SCN-ENV-THMFAIL Thermal control failure
    STATEMENT: Required environmental scenarios: cold start, hot start, ambient temperature cycling,
    high relative humidity, low relative humidity, high altitude, reduced atmospheric
    oxygen, and thermal control failure.

    Environmental cases SHALL include US12308414B2 25 C / 1 atm reference, EP4602674A1
    303 K KOH reference, high-humidity flooding of GDE, low-humidity dry-out, and
    reduced pO2.
     COMMENT: Each listed scenario has a unique IA-SCN-ENV-* ID, Python scenario function, and notebook.
    • IA-SCN-ENV-COLD
      6.1. Cold start UID: IA-SCN-ENV-COLD STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-011 Environmental scenarios
      STATEMENT: Start from a cold soaked initial temperature.
       COMMENT: Temperatures rise toward a warmer operating band under load or heaters if modeled.
    • IA-SCN-ENV-HOT
      6.2. Hot start UID: IA-SCN-ENV-HOT STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-011 Environmental scenarios
      STATEMENT: Start from an elevated soaked temperature.
       COMMENT: Initial temperatures are above T_REF_K and remain within validity limits or are flagged.
    • IA-SCN-ENV-TAMP
      6.3. Ambient temperature cycling UID: IA-SCN-ENV-TAMP STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-011 Environmental scenarios
      STATEMENT: Apply a cyclic ambient temperature boundary.
       COMMENT: Enclosure or cell temperature lags the ambient cycle.
    • IA-SCN-ENV-HIGHRH
      6.4. High relative humidity UID: IA-SCN-ENV-HIGHRH STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-011 Environmental scenarios
      STATEMENT: Supply high-humidity air.
       COMMENT: Gas humidity state increases relative to a dry-air case.
    • IA-SCN-ENV-LOWRH
      6.5. Low relative humidity UID: IA-SCN-ENV-LOWRH STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-011 Environmental scenarios
      STATEMENT: Supply dry air.
       COMMENT: Electrolyte or GDL water is more depleted than the high-RH case.
    • IA-SCN-ENV-ALT
      6.6. High altitude UID: IA-SCN-ENV-ALT STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-011 Environmental scenarios
      STATEMENT: Reduce ambient pressure.
       COMMENT: Inlet oxygen partial pressure is lower than the sea-level reference.
    • IA-SCN-ENV-LOWO2
      6.7. Reduced atmospheric oxygen UID: IA-SCN-ENV-LOWO2 STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-011 Environmental scenarios
      STATEMENT: Reduce inlet O2 mole fraction.
       COMMENT: Discharge capability is reduced versus 0.21 mole fraction air.
    • IA-SCN-ENV-THMFAIL
      6.8. Thermal control failure UID: IA-SCN-ENV-THMFAIL STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-011 Environmental scenarios
      STATEMENT: Disable cooling while load continues.
       COMMENT: Temperatures rise above the cooled reference. Protection may trip.
    IA-NBK-012
    1.6. Mechanical fault scenarios UID: IA-NBK-012 STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Child):
    • IA-SCN-MCH-FAN Fan failure
    • IA-SCN-MCH-PUMP Pump failure
    • IA-SCN-MCH-FILTER Filter blockage
    • IA-SCN-MCH-VALVE Valve failure
    • IA-SCN-MCH-LEAK Electrolyte leak
    • IA-SCN-MCH-RESDEP Reservoir depletion
    • IA-SCN-MCH-CIRC Reduced circulation
    • IA-SCN-MCH-HEX Heat exchanger failure
    • IA-SCN-MCH-VENT Ventilation failure
    STATEMENT: Required mechanical fault scenarios: fan failure, pump failure, filter blockage,
    valve failure, electrolyte leak, reservoir depletion, reduced circulation, heat
    exchanger failure, and ventilation failure.

    Mechanical faults SHALL include loss of sparge/air supply to submerged ORR, ORR
    flooding versus dry-out, lid-vent blockage, and primary-vessel leak into secondary
    containment (US12308414B2 vessel cavity 161).
     COMMENT: Each listed scenario has a unique IA-SCN-MCH-* ID, Python scenario function, and notebook.
    • IA-SCN-MCH-FAN
      7.1. Fan failure UID: IA-SCN-MCH-FAN STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-012 Mechanical fault scenarios
      STATEMENT: Force fan speed toward zero during operation.
       COMMENT: Airflow and O2 delivery fall. Discharge voltage penalty increases.
    • IA-SCN-MCH-PUMP
      7.2. Pump failure UID: IA-SCN-MCH-PUMP STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-012 Mechanical fault scenarios
      STATEMENT: Force pump speed toward zero.
       COMMENT: Electrolyte circulation collapses.
    • IA-SCN-MCH-FILTER
      7.3. Filter blockage UID: IA-SCN-MCH-FILTER STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-012 Mechanical fault scenarios
      STATEMENT: Increase air-path resistance.
       COMMENT: Airflow falls for the same fan command.
    • IA-SCN-MCH-VALVE
      7.4. Valve failure UID: IA-SCN-MCH-VALVE STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-012 Mechanical fault scenarios
      STATEMENT: Hold a valve at a failed position.
       COMMENT: Flow does not follow the commanded position.
    • IA-SCN-MCH-LEAK
      7.5. Electrolyte leak UID: IA-SCN-MCH-LEAK STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-012 Mechanical fault scenarios
      STATEMENT: Impose a leak mass-flow from the electrolyte circuit.
       COMMENT: Liquid inventory declines.
    • IA-SCN-MCH-RESDEP
      7.6. Reservoir depletion UID: IA-SCN-MCH-RESDEP STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-012 Mechanical fault scenarios
      STATEMENT: Operate until reservoir inventory approaches empty.
       COMMENT: An invalid or empty-reservoir condition is reported before negative mass.
    • IA-SCN-MCH-CIRC
      7.7. Reduced circulation UID: IA-SCN-MCH-CIRC STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-012 Mechanical fault scenarios
      STATEMENT: Command a reduced pump flow.
       COMMENT: Circulation flow is lower than the design case.
    • IA-SCN-MCH-HEX
      7.8. Heat exchanger failure UID: IA-SCN-MCH-HEX STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-012 Mechanical fault scenarios
      STATEMENT: Reduce heat-exchanger UA toward zero.
       COMMENT: Cooling heat transfer falls versus the healthy HEX case.
    • IA-SCN-MCH-VENT
      7.9. Ventilation failure UID: IA-SCN-MCH-VENT STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-012 Mechanical fault scenarios
      STATEMENT: Disable enclosure ventilation.
       COMMENT: Enclosure gas inventories of H2 or heat rise relative to ventilated operation.

    1.7. Electrical scenarios UID: IA-NBK-013 STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Child):
    • IA-SCN-ELC-SHORT Cell short
    • IA-SCN-ELC-OC Cell open circuit
    • IA-SCN-ELC-IMBAL Cell imbalance
    • IA-SCN-ELC-MISMATCH Stack mismatch

    • IA-SCN-ELC-OV DC bus overvoltage
    • IA-SCN-ELC-ILIM Inverter current limit

    STATEMENT: Required electrical scenarios: cell short, cell open circuit, cell imbalance, stack
    mismatch, converter overload, DC bus undervoltage, DC bus overvoltage, inverter
    current limit, and sensor failure.

    Electrical scenarios SHALL include can-negative housing contact faults, ORR/OER
    toggle-switch stuck states, and stacked-vessel series-contact opens
    (US12308414B2 Claims 3, 5, 16).
     COMMENT: Each listed scenario has a unique IA-SCN-ELC-* ID, Python scenario function, and notebook.
    • IA-SCN-ELC-SHORT
      8.1. Cell short UID: IA-SCN-ELC-SHORT STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-013 Electrical scenarios
      STATEMENT: Impose a low-resistance cell short.
       COMMENT: Faulted cell voltage collapses and local heating increases.
    • IA-SCN-ELC-OC
      8.2. Cell open circuit UID: IA-SCN-ELC-OC STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-013 Electrical scenarios
      STATEMENT: Open a cell in a series string.
       COMMENT: String current falls to ~0 or the open-cell path is flagged.
    • IA-SCN-ELC-IMBAL
      8.3. Cell imbalance UID: IA-SCN-ELC-IMBAL STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-013 Electrical scenarios
      STATEMENT: Initialize cells at different SOC.
       COMMENT: Cell voltages differ at the same string current.
    • IA-SCN-ELC-MISMATCH
      8.4. Stack mismatch UID: IA-SCN-ELC-MISMATCH STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-013 Electrical scenarios
      STATEMENT: Operate paralleled or series stacks with mismatched capacity or resistance.
       COMMENT: Current sharing is unequal.
    • IA-SCN-ELC-CNVOVL
      8.5. Converter overload UID: IA-SCN-ELC-CNVOVL STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-013 Electrical scenarios
      STATEMENT: Command converter current above rating.
       COMMENT: Current is limited to the rated value or a protection trip occurs.
    • IA-SCN-ELC-UV
      8.6. DC bus undervoltage UID: IA-SCN-ELC-UV STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-013 Electrical scenarios
      STATEMENT: Drive DC-link voltage below the undervoltage threshold.
       COMMENT: Protection or limiter responds at the documented UV setpoint.
    • IA-SCN-ELC-OV
      8.7. DC bus overvoltage UID: IA-SCN-ELC-OV STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-013 Electrical scenarios
      STATEMENT: Drive DC-link voltage above the overvoltage threshold.
       COMMENT: Protection or limiter responds at the documented OV setpoint.
    • IA-SCN-ELC-ILIM
      8.8. Inverter current limit UID: IA-SCN-ELC-ILIM STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-013 Electrical scenarios
      STATEMENT: Command inverter current above the limit.
       COMMENT: Delivered current does not exceed the limit except for documented transient overshoot.
    • IA-SCN-ELC-SENSOR
      8.9. Sensor failure UID: IA-SCN-ELC-SENSOR STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-013 Electrical scenarios
      STATEMENT: Inject sensor bias, stuck, or noise faults.
       COMMENT: Estimator and controller use the failed measurement, not the hidden true plant state.

    as framed in US12308414B2 Background and FIGS. 94-102.

    • IA-SCN-GRD-SWELL
      9.2. Grid voltage swell UID: IA-SCN-GRD-SWELL STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-014 Grid scenarios

      9.4. Overfrequency UID: IA-SCN-GRD-OF STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-014 Grid scenarios
      STATEMENT: Apply a grid overfrequency input.

      9.5. Frequency-watt response UID: IA-SCN-GRD-FW STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-014 Grid scenarios

    STATEMENT: Required long-term scenarios: 100-hour discharge, multiple-day energy dispatch,
    charge/discharge cycling, seasonal storage, calendar aging, cycle aging, capacity
    fade, efficiency degradation, and annual operating profile.

    Long-term scenarios SHALL include 100 h and 300 h discharges, summer-to-winter
    seasonal storage of surplus solar, and calendar aging of replaceable electrodes
    (US12308414B2 Definitions and replaceable-electrode discussion).
     COMMENT: Each listed scenario has a unique IA-SCN-LT-* ID, Python scenario function, and notebook.
    • IA-SCN-LT-100H

       COMMENT: Uses the same ParameterSet as short-horizon discharge, with fidelity settings documented.
    • IA-SCN-LT-DISPATCH
      10.2. Multiple-day energy dispatch UID: IA-SCN-LT-DISPATCH STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):

      10.4. Seasonal storage UID: IA-SCN-LT-SEASON STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-015 Long-term scenarios
      STATEMENT: Hold energy over a seasonal horizon using reduced-order options as needed.

    • IA-SCN-LT-CAL
      10.5. Calendar aging UID: IA-SCN-LT-CAL STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-015 Long-term scenarios
      STATEMENT: Age at rest.
       COMMENT: Capacity or resistance changes with time at zero cycling current.
    • IA-SCN-LT-CYCAGE
      10.6. Cycle aging UID: IA-SCN-LT-CYCAGE STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-015 Long-term scenarios
      STATEMENT: Age under cycling.

    STATEMENT: Required characterization scenarios: current-voltage polarization curves,
    charge/discharge voltage versus SOC, efficiency versus power, efficiency versus
    temperature, SOC versus time, oxygen demand versus power, hydrogen generation versus
    charge current, KOH concentration sweep, thermal response, parameter sensitivity,
    and uncertainty analysis.

    Characterization SHALL include planar versus interdigitated discharge voltage
    versus capacity (EP4602674A1 FIG. 27), coulombic efficiency versus charge time
    (FIGS. 19, 21, 23, 25), and area-specific resistance versus time (FIGS. 20, 22,
    24, 26) at documented 6 M KOH and 303 K.
     COMMENT: Each listed scenario has a unique IA-SCN-CHR-* ID, Python scenario function, and notebook.
    • IA-SCN-CHR-IV
      11.1. Current-voltage polarization UID: IA-SCN-CHR-IV STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-016 Characterization scenarios
      STATEMENT: Sweep current and record voltage.
       COMMENT: Discharge branch voltage decreases with increasing current magnitude.
    • IA-SCN-CHR-VSOC
      11.2. Voltage versus SOC UID: IA-SCN-CHR-VSOC STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-016 Characterization scenarios
      STATEMENT: Record charge and discharge voltage versus SOC.
       COMMENT: Charge voltage lies above discharge voltage at the same SOC for nonzero current.
    • IA-SCN-CHR-EFFP
      11.3. Efficiency versus power UID: IA-SCN-CHR-EFFP STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-016 Characterization scenarios
      STATEMENT: Compute round-trip or one-way efficiency versus power.
       COMMENT: Efficiency is in (0, 1] for finite nonzero power.
    • IA-SCN-CHR-EFFT
      11.4. Efficiency versus temperature UID: IA-SCN-CHR-EFFT STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-016 Characterization scenarios
      STATEMENT: Sweep temperature and compute efficiency.
       COMMENT: Results stay within the property-model temperature domain.
    • IA-SCN-CHR-SOCT
      11.5. SOC versus time UID: IA-SCN-CHR-SOCT STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-016 Characterization scenarios
      STATEMENT: Record SOC(t) for a documented load.
       COMMENT: SOC is in [0, 1] and consistent with Faraday accounting.
    • IA-SCN-CHR-O2P
      11.6. Oxygen demand versus power UID: IA-SCN-CHR-O2P STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-016 Characterization scenarios
      STATEMENT: Compute O2 molar demand versus discharge power.
       COMMENT: O2 demand increases with discharge power under ORR Faraday accounting.
    • IA-SCN-CHR-H2I
      11.7. Hydrogen generation versus charge current UID: IA-SCN-CHR-H2I STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-016 Characterization scenarios
      STATEMENT: Compute H2 rate versus charge current.
       COMMENT: H2 rate is nonnegative and increases with more severe charge polarization.
    • IA-SCN-CHR-KOH
      11.8. KOH concentration sweep UID: IA-SCN-CHR-KOH STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-016 Characterization scenarios

       COMMENT: Conductivity and Nernst potentials vary with concentration. Domain errors are raised outside range.
    • IA-SCN-CHR-THM
      11.9. Thermal response characterization UID: IA-SCN-CHR-THM STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-016 Characterization scenarios
      STATEMENT: Record temperature response to a load step.
       COMMENT: Temperature rises under dissipative load in an undercooled configuration.
    • IA-SCN-CHR-SENS
      11.10. Parameter sensitivity UID: IA-SCN-CHR-SENS STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-016 Characterization scenarios
      STATEMENT: Perturb selected parameters and record output change.
       COMMENT: Sensitivity results identify which parameters were perturbed and their source_class.
    • IA-SCN-CHR-UNC
      11.11. Uncertainty analysis UID: IA-SCN-CHR-UNC STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-016 Characterization scenarios
      STATEMENT: Propagate documented parameter uncertainties with a fixed random seed.
       COMMENT: Results are reproducible given the same seed and parameter uncertainty data.
    • IA-TP-006
      2.3. Scenario verification objectives UID: IA-TP-006 STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-NBK-016 Characterization scenarios
      STATEMENT: The scenario suite SHALL include IA-SCN-PAT-* cases for stacked ORR, DRI bed,

      ORR, spiral, pleated, and adjustable pO2.

      Each scenario SHALL remain a software verification case: conservation, mode

      STATEMENT: Required charge scenarios: constant-current, constant-power, constant-voltage,
      charge tapering, partial charge, charge termination, overcharge protection,
      low-temperature charging, high-temperature charging, charging with hydrogen
      evolution, and charging with limited electrolyte circulation.

      Charge current greater than 6 mA/g to at least twice rated capacity SHALL be an
      allowed formation/full-charge protocol (EP4602674A1 [0261]). Dual-electrode charge
      SHALL use the OER path (EP4602674A1 [0049]).
       RATIONALE: US12308414B2 rechargeable metal-air operation; EP4602674A1 charge through OER and
      HER competition on thick iron electrodes.
       COMMENT: Each listed scenario has a unique IA-SCN-CHG-* ID, Python scenario function, notebook,
      and seaborn plots.

      STATEMENT: Required discharge scenarios: constant-current, constant-power, variable-load,
      partial discharge, deep discharge, oxygen-limited, thermal-limited, high-rate,
      low-rate, and 100-hour discharge.

      Discharge SHALL use the ORR path (EP4602674A1 [0049]). 100 h and 300 h discharges
      SHALL be available, corresponding to about 3-5 cm and 4-6 cm anode thickness in
      US12308414B2. Oxygen-limited discharge SHALL include restricted pO2 within
      0.01-100 atm (US12308414B2).
       RATIONALE: US12308414B2 duration versus anode thickness; EP4602674A1 dual-electrode discharge
      to Fe(OH)2 / Fe3O4.
       COMMENT: Each listed scenario has a unique IA-SCN-DCH-* ID, Python scenario function, and notebook.

      • IA-SCN-DCH-100H 100-hour discharge
      STATEMENT: Required discharge scenarios: constant-current, constant-power, variable-load,
      partial discharge, deep discharge, oxygen-limited, thermal-limited, high-rate,
      low-rate, and 100-hour discharge.

      Discharge SHALL use the ORR path (EP4602674A1 [0049]). 100 h and 300 h discharges
      SHALL be available, corresponding to about 3-5 cm and 4-6 cm anode thickness in
      US12308414B2. Oxygen-limited discharge SHALL include restricted pO2 within
      0.01-100 atm (US12308414B2).
       RATIONALE: US12308414B2 duration versus anode thickness; EP4602674A1 dual-electrode discharge
      to Fe(OH)2 / Fe3O4.
       COMMENT: Each listed scenario has a unique IA-SCN-DCH-* ID, Python scenario function, and notebook.

      1.6. Mechanical fault scenarios UID: IA-NBK-012 STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Child):
      • IA-SCN-MCH-FAN Fan failure
      • IA-SCN-MCH-PUMP Pump failure

      STATEMENT: Required mechanical fault scenarios: fan failure, pump failure, filter blockage,

      exchanger failure, and ventilation failure.

      Mechanical faults SHALL include loss of sparge/air supply to submerged ORR, ORR
      flooding versus dry-out, lid-vent blockage, and primary-vessel leak into secondary
      containment (US12308414B2 vessel cavity 161).
       COMMENT: Each listed scenario has a unique IA-SCN-MCH-* ID, Python scenario function, and notebook.

      • IA-SCN-MCH-LEAK Electrolyte leak
      • IA-SCN-MCH-RESDEP Reservoir depletion
      • IA-SCN-MCH-CIRC Reduced circulation
      • IA-SCN-MCH-HEX Heat exchanger failure
      • IA-SCN-MCH-VENT Ventilation failure
      STATEMENT: Required mechanical fault scenarios: fan failure, pump failure, filter blockage,
      valve failure, electrolyte leak, reservoir depletion, reduced circulation, heat
      exchanger failure, and ventilation failure.

      Mechanical faults SHALL include loss of sparge/air supply to submerged ORR, ORR
      flooding versus dry-out, lid-vent blockage, and primary-vessel leak into secondary
      containment (US12308414B2 vessel cavity 161).

    SEC-SSS3-PAT

    12. Patent-architecture scenarios

     UID: SEC-SSS3-PAT
    These scenarios map US12308414B2 Claims 1-18 and EP4602674A1 Claims 1, 20, 38, 55,
    70, 77, and FIGS. 19-27 onto executable ironair scenario functions.
    • IA-SYS-009
      3.1. Submerged stacked ORR with depth-equalized pressure drop UID: IA-SYS-009 STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-SYS-002 Integrated physics simulation
      RELATIONS (Child):
      • IA-SDD-008 ORR geometric modes
      • IA-SCN-PAT-STACKORR Submerged stacked ORR equal pressure drop
      • IA-TD-008 Stacked ORR equal pressure-drop test
      • IA-TP-005 Architecture verification objectives
      STATEMENT: The system SHALL support a submerged ORR electrode comprising a series of discrete
      ORR electrode sections arranged vertically in a stack below the electrolyte
      surface.

      Each discrete ORR section SHALL have geometry that can vary with depth below the
      electrolyte surface.

      The air-path model SHALL be able to impose equal pressure drop across each stacked
      ORR section in the depth direction.

      This configuration SHALL be the default representation of US12308414B2 Claim 1.
       RATIONALE: US12308414B2 Claim 1. Detailed description FIGS. 25A-36B, 57-58, and 35A-35C
      describe stacked-core / distillation-column ORR layers with depth-dependent bubble
      thickness, baffles, and cascading air.
       COMMENT: Equal pressure drop is an algebraic hydraulic constitutive law, not an artificial
      dynamic lag (IA-SYS-003).
    IA-SCN-PAT-STACKORR
    12.1. Submerged stacked ORR equal pressure drop UID: IA-SCN-PAT-STACKORR STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
    • IA-SYS-009 Submerged stacked ORR with depth-equalized pressure drop
    STATEMENT: Operate a vertical stack of discrete submerged ORR sections with depth-dependent
    geometry and equal pressure drop in the depth direction (US12308414B2 Claim 1).
    Record air utilization, pO2, and ORR current versus height.
     COMMENT: Pressure drop across each stacked section is the same. Bubble cascade reaches
    upper sections. No external electrolyte leak is required for internal flooding.
    • IA-SYS-013
      3.5. Can-negative housing and DRI pellet anode UID: IA-SYS-013 STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-SYS-002 Integrated physics simulation
      RELATIONS (Child):
      • IA-SCN-PAT-DRI DRI pellet bed anode
      STATEMENT: The metal electrode SHALL be modelable as a bed of direct reduced iron (DRI)
      pellets or marbles (US12308414B2 Claim 18; FIG. 3 packed bed).

      A housing-as-current-conductor (can-negative) configuration SHALL be supported in
      which the vessel conducts anode current (Claim 5; FIG. 11). Housing materials
      SHALL include polymers (polyethylene, HDPE, UHMW, polypropylene) and metals
      (nickel, steel, anodized aluminum, nickel-coated steel or aluminum) as parameters.

      The metal electrode position relative to ORR and OER SHALL be changeable
      (Claim 13; FIG. 52 movable anode).
       RATIONALE: US12308414B2 Claims 5, 13, and 18. DRI beds provide low-cost iron inventory for
      LODES. Can-negative stacked housings enable gravity-driven series connections.
    IA-SCN-PAT-DRI
    12.2. DRI pellet bed anode UID: IA-SCN-PAT-DRI STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
    • IA-SYS-013 Can-negative housing and DRI pellet anode
    STATEMENT: Discharge and charge a packed bed of direct reduced iron pellets
    (US12308414B2 Claim 18; FIG. 3) in 6 M KOH.
     COMMENT: Iron inventory oxidizes to Fe(OH)2 / Fe3O4 on discharge. Pellet-bed porosity
    absorbs discharge volume increase (EP4602674A1 [0043]).
    • IA-CHM-011
      3.11. Coulombic efficiency versus electrode architecture UID: IA-CHM-011 STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-SYS-015 Channeled iron electrode with interdigitated OER
      RELATIONS (Child):
      • IA-SCN-PAT-INTERDIG Interdigitated OER versus planar control
      • IA-TD-009 Interdigitated coulombic-efficiency trend test
      STATEMENT: The chemistry-to-electrode coupling SHALL report instantaneous coulombic charge
      efficiency as the fraction of charge current stored in intended iron reduction
      products rather than HER (EP4602674A1 [0044], FIGS. 19, 21, 23, 25).

      Planar, channeled, and interdigitated OER/iron layouts SHALL be comparable on
      the same ParameterSet. Interdigitated layouts SHALL be able to show higher
      coulombic efficiency and lower sensitivity of efficiency to areal loading than
      planar layouts, matching the qualitative simulation results of EP4602674A1
      FIGS. 19-24 at 6 M KOH, 303 K, initial rib porosity 0.6, example ChanFrac 0.4,
      w_rib 5 mm, and example loading 4 g Fe/cm2.
       RATIONALE: EP4602674A1 [0261]-[0280] and FIGS. 19-27. FIG. 27 experimental interdigitated
      cell showed an extended upper discharge voltage plateau versus planar control
      at matched loading, temperature, current, electrolyte, and ORR.
    IA-SCN-PAT-INTERDIG
    12.3. Interdigitated OER versus planar control UID: IA-SCN-PAT-INTERDIG STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
    • IA-CHM-011 Coulombic efficiency versus electrode architecture
    STATEMENT: Compare planar iron/OER, channeled iron with planar OER, and channeled iron with
    interdigitated OER at 6 M KOH, 303 K, initial rib porosity 0.6, ChanFrac 0.4,
    w_rib 5 mm, and 4 g Fe/cm2 (EP4602674A1 FIGS. 19-27).
     COMMENT: Interdigitated configuration shows higher coulombic efficiency and an extended
    upper discharge voltage plateau relative to planar, matching FIG. 27 qualitative
    behavior. Software comparison is verification against the disclosed trends, not
    reproduction of unpublished experimental tables.
    • IA-SYS-007
      2.1. Long-duration energy storage mission UID: IA-SYS-007 STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-SYS-002 Integrated physics simulation
      RELATIONS (Child):
      • IA-ODE-006 Multiscale execution
      • IA-GRD-001 Grid interface ODE
      • IA-SCN-PAT-ASYM Asymmetric 100 h charge and 300 h discharge
      STATEMENT: The system SHALL model grid-connected LODES operation with energy storage durations
      of 8 hours or longer, including 8 h, 8-20 h, 20 h, 20-24 h, 24 h, week-scale, and
      seasonal (multi-day to multi-month) windows as defined in US12308414B2 (long
      duration / ultra-long duration; LODES).

      Anode thickness and independent charge versus discharge length scales SHALL be
      parameterizable so that example durations disclosed in US12308414B2 can be
      represented: about 3-5 cm anode thickness for about 100 h; about 4-6 cm for about
      300 h; and an asymmetric example of about 100 h charge with about 300 h discharge
      for a 5 cm by 5 cm square anode cross-section.
       RATIONALE: US12308414B2 Definitions and Detailed Description (anode thickness versus duration;
      symmetric versus asymmetric duration). EP4602674A1 [0002] and [0045] motivate thick
      high-areal-capacity iron electrodes to amortize air-electrode cost.
       COMMENT: Default demonstration discharge of 100 h (3.6e5 s) is the short end of the patented
      LODES range, not a claim that hardware has been validated at that duration.
    IA-SCN-PAT-ASYM
    12.4. Asymmetric 100 h charge and 300 h discharge UID: IA-SCN-PAT-ASYM STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
    • IA-SYS-007 Long-duration energy storage mission
    STATEMENT: Configure independent charge and discharge length scales for about 100 h charge
    and about 300 h discharge with a 5 cm by 5 cm anode cross-section
    (US12308414B2 asymmetric-duration example).
     COMMENT: Charge duration and discharge duration are independently tunable. SOC and Faraday
    accounting remain consistent over both windows.
    • IA-SYS-012
      3.4. ORR geometry and inverse air-breathing options UID: IA-SYS-012 STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-SYS-002 Integrated physics simulation
      RELATIONS (Child):
      • IA-ORR-001 Oxygen reduction ODE
      • IA-SCN-PAT-FLOAT Floating ORR with submerged OER
      STATEMENT: The ORR component SHALL support the following patented geometries as selectable
      configurations, each identified in metadata:

      - wavy or rippled ORR to increase triple-phase boundary at a given footprint
      (US12308414B2 Claim 4; FIGS. 10A-10C);
      - frame that displaces electrolyte to create a gas volume at depth (Claim 7);
      - box configuration filled with air (Claim 8; FIGS. 14-16 inverse air-breathing);
      - supplied-air ORR (Claim 9);
      - curved ORR (Claim 10);
      - frame trapping supplied air in an air chamber bounded by the ORR surface
      (Claim 11);
      - tube-shaped ORR, including circular, oval, teardrop, or polygonal tubes
      (Claim 12; FIGS. 20A-23, 59-62);
      - floating ORR at the electrolyte free surface with submerged OER (Summary;
      FIGS. 1B-3);
      - vertical natural-air-breathing ORR (FIGS. 4A-8);
      - convex oxygen-pocket submerged ORR (FIGS. 17-19B);
      - open-bottom inverse air-breathing ORR (FIG. 24);
      - helical/auger ORR (FIG. 44);
      - rectilinear parallel-plate ORR stacks (FIGS. 45-47B);
      - coaxial cylindrical ORR core with hexagonal anode/OER tube (FIGS. 27-34).
       RATIONALE: US12308414B2 Claims 4 and 7-12 plus detailed-description architectures. Inverse
      air-breathing submerges ORR so leaks remain internal to the cell.
    IA-SCN-PAT-FLOAT
    12.5. Floating ORR with submerged OER UID: IA-SCN-PAT-FLOAT STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
    • IA-SYS-012 ORR geometry and inverse air-breathing options
    STATEMENT: Float the ORR at the electrolyte free surface while the OER remains submerged
    (US12308414B2 Summary; FIGS. 1B-3). Vary electrolyte height by evaporation and
    confirm the ORR remains at the triple-phase boundary.
     COMMENT: ORR follows the free surface. OER remains wetted. Flooding and dry-out flags stay
    clear under slow height change.
    • IA-SYS-017
      4.3. Discrete anodes, discrete OER cathodes, spiral, and pleated layouts UID: IA-SYS-017 STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-SYS-015 Channeled iron electrode with interdigitated OER
      RELATIONS (Child):

      • IA-SCN-PAT-PLEAT Pleated iron and OER
      STATEMENT: The system SHALL support these additional EP4602674A1 independent architectures as

      - plurality of anodes separated by channels, electrically communicating, with
      interdigitated OER (Claim 20; FIG. 12);
      - plurality of OER cathodes interdigitated with the anode array and electrically
      communicating with each other (Claim 38);
      - iron electrode with channels and a plurality of OER cathodes in the channels
      (Claim 55);
      - spiral iron electrode and anode current collector with spiral OER at least
      partially bifilar, ORR facing the spiral axis (Claim 70);
      - pleated iron electrode and pleated OER with channels between pleats (Claim 77;
      FIG. 17), optionally with OER on both faces of the iron electrode (Claim 80).

      Double-sided cells across a shared current collector (Claim 18; FIGS. 6-8) and
      paired cells sharing an air channel between ORR backsides (Claim 19; FIGS. 9-11)
      SHALL be supported.
       RATIONALE: EP4602674A1 independent Claims 20, 38, 55, 70, 77 and dependent Claims 18-19.

    • IA-SYS-022
      5.3. Temperature, pressure, and oxygen partial pressure UID: IA-SYS-022 STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
      • IA-SYS-002 Integrated physics simulation
      RELATIONS (Child):
      • IA-SCN-PAT-PO2 Adjustable oxygen partial pressure
      STATEMENT: Unless a scenario states otherwise, property evaluations SHALL use room temperature
      25 C and standard ambient pressure 1 atm as defined in US12308414B2
      ("room temperature is 25 C"; "standard temperature and pressure is 25 C and
      1 atmosphere"). The term "about" SHALL mean a variance of plus or minus 10 percent
      or the larger of instrument error, per that patent.

      Gas-phase oxygen partial pressure SHALL be parameterizable from 0.01 atm to 100 atm
      on discharge and from 0.001 atm to 100 atm on charge, and MAY be raised on
      discharge and lowered on charge to increase thermodynamic driving force
      (US12308414B2 pressurized-gas paragraph).

      EP4602674A1 simulation reference of 6 M KOH at 303 K SHALL be an available
      property-model operating point.
       RATIONALE: US12308414B2 definitions and pO2 operating window; EP4602674A1 FIGS. 19-26
      simulation conditions.
    IA-SCN-PAT-PO2
    12.8. Adjustable oxygen partial pressure UID: IA-SCN-PAT-PO2 STATUS: Active RELATIONS (Parent):
    • IA-SYS-022 Temperature, pressure, and oxygen partial pressure
    STATEMENT: Raise pO2 on discharge within 0.01-100 atm and lower pO2 on charge within
    0.001-100 atm (US12308414B2 pressurized-gas paragraph).
     COMMENT: Discharge driving force increases with pO2. Charge OER is not forced to high pO2.
    Solver remains within property-model domain.
